text: Now that the glossary and dictionary exist, Risk and Compliance lead Amara Chen classifies which of these elements are actually sensitive.

Four tiers: Public, safe for anyone. Internal, safe for employees only. Confidential, limited to the people who need it for their job. Restricted, limited to a named, audited group, with a formal breach response.

SKU and Order Total land Internal — commercially sensitive, not personal. Customer email lands Confidential — the exact element behind the Lesson 1 access request. Payment card token lands Restricted — still PCI scope even as a token.

The pass also turns up an element nobody had flagged: date of birth, captured during warranty registration for age-restricted gear. It gets the same Confidential tier as email, and a note to reconsider it as a fifth critical data element.
Next: Lesson 7 writes real T-SQL quality checks, and that work starts with these same classified, defined elements.
